title: Auto Captions Need Punctuation: Check the Meaning First
description: Punctuate auto captions according to the spoken meaning, rather than adding a full stop at every caption break.
direct: Correct punctuation by listening to the whole sentence. A comma or question mark can change what the viewer thinks the speaker meant.
figureAlt: Photographic caption proofreading desk with a video camera in background and two large paper sentence cards: “Let’s eat Sam” and “Let’s eat, Sam”

cards.choice.heading: Start with the decision
cards.choice.body: “Let’s eat, Sam” addresses Sam; “Let’s eat Sam” says something different. The example is deliberately simple, but it shows why punctuation review belongs beside spelling review. A caption card ending does not necessarily mean that the speaker finished a sentence.
sections.detail-0.heading: Keep the words faithful
sections.detail-0.body: Do not change a speaker’s intended meaning just to make a sentence look tidier. Hesitation and informal speech may need careful judgment. Section508.gov identifies grammar, punctuation and awkward line breaks as common auto-caption problems and recommends editing the result. This small review does not by itself certify a video as accessible.
sections.detail-1.heading: Know which tools are online
sections.detail-1.body: Transcript editing is supported; optional AI Correct uses the internet after consent. Core captions can run on device. Free single-video exports include the app watermark, while Pro removes it. The illustrated sentences are an invented teaching example, not an actual transcription error or an app screenshot.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Should every pause become a comma?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: No. Use punctuation to show the speaker’s meaning and grouping. A pause can also come from a breath or hesitation.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Should I automatically add a period where each caption disappears?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Only when a sentence actually ends. Read the next caption as well and avoid turning a continuing thought into separate sentences.

steps.step-1.text: Generate captions in Subtitle Maker: Just Captions, then listen to a complete sentence while reading the transcript.
steps.step-2.text: Edit punctuation and capitalization to match the thought. If you choose optional AI Correct, review its suggestions against the audio before keeping them.
steps.step-3.text: Preview and export the captioned video. Watch the saved copy at phone size and check that sentence endings, questions and quotations still read naturally.
